summary: Authenticated browser capture proved the shopping-list invite write: POST /data/shopping-lists/share-list with a multipart field named operation carrying an ordinary string part containing protobuf bytes. The outer message contains metadata (field 1), list ID (field 2), and target email (field 4). Removal, stop-sharing, and household-user writes remain fail-closed because their payloads were not captured.

multipart_field.name: operation
multipart_field.shape: ordinary string multipart part with no Content-Type header; not application/octet-stream and not JSON

request_payload_layout.field_1: length-delimited PBOperationMetadata with fresh operationId, handlerId share-shopping-list, and authenticated userId
request_payload_layout.field_3: absent in the capture and never populated

response.gating: non-OK HTTP, non-zero statusCode, or any errorTitle/errorMessage is rejected; HTTP 200 alone is not success

live_capture.fresh_read: The authenticated UI showed the list still present and displayed the unregistered invite as pending. AnyList's fresh data may contain an email-only shared-user pair for that pending invite; the CLI requires a non-empty stable user ID before reporting an accepted share.

cleanup.fixture: disposable list created solely for the probe
cleanup.fixture_removal: removed through the already verified remove-shopping-list operation and confirmed absent by fresh read
cleanup.invite_side_effect: the pending invite itself has no captured retract route; it targeted a redacted address on the disposable fixture and no account or list identifiers are recorded

gate_state: Invite-add is live-proven and enabled through lists sharing add; preview is default and --apply is required. Removal, stop-sharing, and household-user writes remain fail-closed.
verification: client tests assert the exact route, ordinary operation part, protobuf field set, response gating, and byte-for-byte 401 retry
CLI tests assert preview/default/dry-run/apply gating, exact ID or unique-name resolution, and honest pending-versus-accepted wording
no live request is made by unit tests; this record is the only live evidence
invariants_held: No real email, account identifier, cookie, token, or raw captured body is stored
HTTP 200 alone is never reported as acceptance
A pending invitation is never represented as an accepted shared user
Unproven removal, stop-sharing, and household-user operations remain fail-closed
